note: Discovery leads for introduction-to-business topic workers (phase 2). LITERACY level: teach what businesses are and how they work — no accounting/finance depth (those are separate subjects), no legal how-to. Legal forms are described as general concepts with their defining trade-offs; laws vary by jurisdiction — never state jurisdiction-specific rules as universal.

cautions: LEGAL FORMS: describe sole proprietorship / partnership / corporation / LLC by their defining trade-offs (liability, taxes, ownership, paperwork) as general concepts. NEVER state jurisdiction-specific rules as universal; if a source is jurisdiction-specific, say so. No legal advice.

SIBLING SUBJECTS: accounting (accounting-basics in THIS subject is the literacy overview — the accounting subject owns depth), finance (same), marketing (same), management-and-leadership (same). Reference only.
ECONOMICS: economics-and-business must stay at literacy level (supply/demand, markets, business cycles as concepts) — no formulas beyond the most basic, no policy positions.
ETHICS: business-ethics teaches frameworks and the general landscape (stakeholders, compliance, reputation) — no political stances, no named-company scandal deep-dives beyond general facts.
GLOBAL BUSINESS: frame as general concepts (import/export, trade, culture) with factual framing — no trade-war advocacy, no country stereotypes.

Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D (≥1 C, ≥1 D per topic; max 3 of 5 per slot). Verify keys from the file yourself. Avoid reusing identical question-stem templates across topics ('Which statement best defines X used in this lesson?' is BANNED — write topic-specific stems).
